title.en: WebXR delivery and desktop fallback boundary

summary: Treat immersive XR as a capability-gated session mode with explicit reference-space, input, lifecycle and equivalent non-XR delivery.
objective: Unsupported, denied, interrupted and completed XR requests all return to a usable non-XR scene without losing semantic state or running a second loop.
intent_signals: keep desktop mode after headset exit
example_prompts: Deliver an interior walkthrough in XR with a desktop alternative.
Gate immersive AR on actual session capability and preserve selection after exit.
Define WebXR reference-space and input ownership without promising universal support.
not_for: Native XR packages outside the Web platform.
Comfort or performance certification without target-device observation.

principles: XR availability is a runtime capability and permission outcome, not an asset property. A valid glTF scene does not establish that an immersive session can start.

Choose reference space, scale, locomotion and interaction rays as delivery semantics. Blender supplies correctly scaled content and authored anchors; the browser session supplies tracked views and inputs.
XR is an enhancement of one application state. Enter, end, denial and device loss must converge on the same owned scene state and one renderer loop, with an equivalent non-XR route to the content.
implementation: Export Blender content with declared metre scale, origin, floor and interaction anchors. Do not bake a headset pose or room boundary into the asset as if it were portable tracking data.

In a secure context, first test navigator.xr and isSessionSupported for the requested mode. Advertise an enter control only as a capability hint; request the session from an eligible user activation, handle rejection, and keep the desktop/static path available.

Enable the Three.js XR manager for the chosen renderer backend, set the intended reference-space type before the session, inject the accepted session through the documented manager path, and drive both XR and non-XR views from the renderer-owned animation loop.

On session end, detach XR-only input, restore the non-XR camera/control policy, preserve declared selection/time state, and avoid creating a second scene or mixer. Embedded deployments also declare the xr-spatial-tracking Permissions Policy relationship.
observable_checks: With navigator.xr absent, unsupported mode, denied request and policy block, the user sees the declared non-XR scene or static equivalent rather than an inert XR button.
Entering and ending XR preserves the selected object and playback time under the declared policy; exactly one animation loop and one application state remain.

A one-metre Blender reference object, declared floor and interaction anchor are inspected in the transported asset and mapped to the chosen reference-space convention; no room-boundary accuracy is inferred.
Runtime capability reporting names browser, requested session mode, reference space and renderer backend/revision; it does not generalize one result to all devices.

creative_affordances: XR locomotion may be teleport, guided viewpoints, room-scale or stationary inspection.
The non-XR path may be an interactive orbit view, annotated views or a static report with equivalent purpose.
known_limits: isSessionSupported may return a false positive by design; requestSession remains authoritative for the attempted session.
No XR hardware/session, renderer backend, input, comfort or performance test was run.

claims.statement: The WebXR Device API is exposed in secure contexts; its application flow queries isSessionSupported, requests an immersive session during transient activation, runs the XR frame loop until shutdown, and notes that support queries may produce false positives. Spatial-tracking sessions are also governed by the xr-spatial-tracking Permissions Policy whose default allowlist is self.
claims.scope: W3C WebXR Candidate Recommendation Draft dated 2026-06-09; actual user agent, hardware, permission and policy outcomes must be tested.

source_refs.locator: Sections 1.2 Application flow, 3 Initialization, 13.8.1 and 14.1 Permissions Policy

claims.statement: Current Three.js WebXRManager documentation says XR support is disabled by default, exposes isPresenting, lets the application set a reference-space type before a session, and accepts an XRSession through setSession to start XR rendering.
claims.scope: Live unversioned Three.js WebXRManager documentation read 2026-09-08; renderer backend and installed revision must be verified.
